facts:
Focus now: Shipping logq 3.0, a command-line tool for querying log files, with plugins and Windows support
Pieces of work:
- Config loader (also called the config file loader): delivered. Settings load from TOML files and environment variables. Changed at this step.
- Query speedups (also called faster queries): being worked on now. The parsed log index is cached on disk between runs. Merged into it: Index cache. Changed at this step.
- Index cache: dropped. Merged into Query speedups. Changed at this step.
- Plugin API (also called plugins): being worked on now. Plugins load and run; the sandbox that limits what a plugin can read is not built yet.
- Windows installer (also called the MSI): being worked on now. The MSI installer builds on a local machine; it is not signed yet.
- ARM Linux build: waits on something outside the session. Waits for the infra team to add an ARM runner to CI.
- Homebrew formula: set aside, not being worked on now. The formula is written; logq installs and runs from it on a local machine.
- Plugin docs: not started yet. A guide to writing plugins; nothing is written yet.
- 3.0 release (also called the 3.0 launch): not started yet. Starts once the Windows installer, which this session builds, is done.
- Release notes: not started yet. Notes on what changed in 3.0; nothing is written yet.
- Color themes: not started yet. Color themes for the query output; nothing is built yet.
- Telemetry opt-out: not started yet. A setting that turns off usage telemetry; nothing is built yet.
- Shell completions: delivered. Completions work in bash, zsh and fish.
- JSON output: delivered. Every command can print JSON.
- Man pages: delivered. Each command has a man page.
Open asks:
- "Publish the formula to the main Homebrew tap, or to a logq tap of our own?" holds up Homebrew formula
Not work:
- rule: No release tags until the Windows installer is signed
- finding: The website's download page still links the 2.x installers; outside this task
Running work:
- Builds the plugin sandbox, for Plugin API
- Signs the Windows installer with the release certificate, for Windows installer
